questions.stem: The emergency department triage nurse is using the Emergency Severity Index (ESI). Which client should the nurse assign to ESI level 1?

options.text: A 45-year-old with crushing chest pain who is pale and sweaty; BP 78/40, HR 128
A 30-year-old with right lower abdominal pain, T 38.3 °C, HR 104, who will need labs and a CT
A 72-year-old with new slurred speech and right-sided weakness that began 40 minutes ago
A 25-year-old with a swollen ankle after a fall who cannot bear weight on it

rationale.correct: ESI 1 means the client needs immediate life-saving intervention for airway, breathing or circulation. High-risk but stable clients, such as a possible stroke, are ESI 2.

perOption.a: ESI 1 is for clients who need immediate life-saving intervention, such as this client in shock.
perOption.b: This client needs several resources and has borderline vital signs, which makes ESI 2 or 3, not 1.
perOption.c: A possible stroke is high-risk (ESI 2) and needs rapid evaluation, but no immediate life-saving intervention.
perOption.d: A stable client who needs one resource, an x-ray, is ESI 4.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A clinic nurse is returning phone calls from clients. Which caller should the nurse tell to call 911 now?

options.text: A client with type 2 diabetes whose glucose is 310 mg/dL who feels thirsty but is not vomiting
A client whose right arm suddenly became weak 20 minutes ago and whose speech is slurred
A client with a migraine like the usual ones that the usual medicine has not relieved
A client with a temperature of 38.6 °C (101.5 °F) and a productive cough for 3 days

rationale.correct: Sudden neurological signs need emergency medical services because time to treatment decides the outcome for stroke.

perOption.a: This client needs same-day advice about correction and fluids, not emergency transport.
perOption.b: Sudden one-sided weakness and slurred speech suggest stroke; emergency services get the client to treatment fastest.
perOption.c: A typical migraine that is not relieved needs advice or a visit; a sudden, worst-ever headache would be different.
perOption.d: This client should be seen today, but stable vital signs make 911 unnecessary.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A home health nurse is planning visits for the day. Which client should the nurse visit first?

options.text: A client with a stage 2 sacral pressure injury who is due for a dressing change today
A client taking warfarin whose gums have bled since morning and who had a nosebleed
A client with heart failure whose weight is 0.5 kg higher than at the visit a week ago
A client with type 2 diabetes who needs teaching about a new glucose meter

rationale.correct: Visit first the client whose condition may be unstable or getting worse, such as bleeding on an anticoagulant.

perOption.a: Routine wound care can be scheduled later in the day.
perOption.b: Bleeding at more than one site on warfarin suggests a high INR and needs prompt assessment and a level.
perOption.c: A small weekly gain needs follow-up but is not urgent; a gain of 1 kg in a day or 2 kg in a week would be.
perOption.d: Teaching a stable client can be done later.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse in a long-term care facility receives four reports from assistive personnel. Which resident should the nurse assess first?

options.text: A resident with Alzheimer disease who is walking up and down the hallway as usual
A resident who refused breakfast and lunch and says the food is tasteless
A resident who is newly confused this morning and has a temperature of 38.4 °C
A resident with COPD whose SpO2 is 89% on room air, the same as the last month

rationale.correct: An acute change from baseline in an older adult, such as new confusion, needs prompt assessment because it may be the only sign of serious illness.

perOption.a: Wandering needs supervision, but it is the resident's usual behavior.
perOption.b: Poor intake needs follow-up today but is not urgent.
perOption.c: An acute change in mental status with fever suggests infection or sepsis in an older adult.
perOption.d: This saturation matches the resident's baseline.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse in the intensive care unit receives four alerts at the same time. Which client needs the nurse's attention first?

options.text: A client on a ventilator whose high-pressure alarm sounds each time the client coughs
A client with an arterial line whose waveform has become dampened in the last hour
A client with a new heart rate of 168/min, blood pressure 84/50, who reports feeling dizzy
A client on a propofol infusion who opens the eyes briefly to voice and then drifts off

rationale.correct: A rhythm that causes hypotension and symptoms is unstable and needs immediate action; equipment alarms with an obvious, harmless cause come later.

perOption.a: Coughing commonly sets off the high-pressure alarm; it settles when the cough stops.
perOption.b: A dampened waveform needs troubleshooting soon but is not life-threatening by itself.
perOption.c: A rapid rhythm with hypotension and symptoms is unstable and may need synchronized cardioversion.
perOption.d: Light sedation that responds to voice is often the target.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The charge nurse reviews the unit board at 0730. Highlight the client situations that need the charge nurse's attention first.

cells: Client 1 day after a hysterectomy; pain 4/10 after an oral analgesic
Client with pneumonia; SpO2 dropped from 95% to 87%, now restless
Client waiting for discharge; ride arrives at 1100
Client on a heparin infusion; aPTT 140 seconds (target 60 to 85)
Client with diabetes; breakfast glucose 178 mg/dL
Client with a hip fracture; new pallor and no pulse in the foot

rationale.correct: Act on new hypoxemia, a dangerous anticoagulation level and loss of circulation before stable findings.

perOption.r2: Acute hypoxemia with restlessness needs immediate assessment.
perOption.r4: A supratherapeutic aPTT puts the client at risk of bleeding; the infusion must be adjusted per protocol now.
perOption.r5: This is treated with correction-scale insulin and is not urgent.
perOption.r6: Signs of arterial compromise need emergency action.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Recognize the most urgent situations on a unit.

questions.stem: The nurse receives four calls at the start of the shift. Place them in the order the nurse should respond, from first to last.

items.text: A client receiving a blood transfusion reports chills and back pain
A client with diabetes reports feeling shaky and sweaty
A client 30 minutes after a thoracentesis reports sudden shortness of breath
A client asks for help to walk to the bathroom

rationale.correct: Breathing first, then an acute transfusion reaction, then hypoglycemia, then routine needs.

perOption.a: A possible pneumothorax is a breathing emergency.
perOption.b: A possible hemolytic reaction: the transfusion must be stopped right away.
perOption.c: Likely hypoglycemia needs prompt treatment, but the first two are more immediately life-threatening.
perOption.d: A safety need, but it can be delegated or met after the urgent calls.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client has just returned to the surgical unit after a bowel resection under general anesthesia. Which finding requires the nurse's immediate action?

options.text: Pain rated 6 out of 10 at the incision
Snoring respirations with an SpO2 of 86%
Shivering with a temperature of 36.0 °C (96.8 °F)
Urine output of 40 mL in the last hour

rationale.correct: An obstructed airway after anesthesia is the priority; jaw thrust, repositioning and oxygen come first.

perOption.a: Pain needs treatment soon but is not the most urgent finding.
perOption.b: Snoring after anesthesia suggests a partly blocked airway; reposition and support the airway now.
perOption.c: Mild hypothermia and shivering are common after surgery and are treated with warming.
perOption.d: This output is adequate.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The RN on a rehabilitation unit is planning which tasks to give to assistive personnel (AP). For each task, choose whether the RN can delegate it to the AP.

rows.text: Helping a stable client with range-of-motion exercises the therapist has taught
Checking a stable client's glucose with a meter, when trained and allowed by policy
Deciding whether a client is ready to walk without a gait belt
Feeding a client with a new swallowing disorder at the first meal
Recording a client's intake and output for the shift

rationale.correct: AP can do routine, standardized tasks for stable clients; the RN keeps assessment, judgment and care of clients with unpredictable needs.

perOption.r1:c1: This is a routine, standardized task for a stable client.
perOption.r2:c1: Point-of-care glucose checks are delegable to trained AP in many facilities; the RN interprets the result.
perOption.r2:c2: It is delegable when the AP is trained and policy allows it.
perOption.r3:c2: Assessment and evaluation cannot be delegated.
perOption.r4:c1: Aspiration risk at the first meal needs a licensed nurse.
perOption.r4:c2: A new dysphagia needs licensed staff until a plan is established.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Decide which tasks to delegate on a rehabilitation unit.

questions.stem: A nurse from a staffing agency is working on an oncology unit for the first time. Which assignment is most appropriate for this nurse?

options.text: A client receiving a first dose of IV chemotherapy this morning
Two stable clients recovering from routine abdominal surgery
The role of charge nurse for the shift
A client with a new tracheostomy who needs frequent suctioning

rationale.correct: Give new or agency staff stable clients with predictable care, and keep high-acuity or unit-specific care with regular staff.

perOption.a: This needs a nurse who knows the unit's chemotherapy protocols and the client's plan.
perOption.b: Stable clients with predictable care suit staff who are new to the unit.
perOption.c: Being charge nurse needs knowledge of the unit, its staff and its resources.
perOption.d: High-acuity care goes to experienced unit staff.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Make safe assignments for agency staff.

questions.stem: The RN is working with an LPN in a long-term care facility. Select the 3 tasks that are appropriate for the RN to assign to the LPN.

options.text: Giving scheduled insulin to a resident with stable diabetes
Doing a sterile dressing change on a healing surgical wound
Reinforcing fall-prevention teaching the RN started
Doing the admission assessment on a new resident
Writing the plan of care for a resident with a new pressure injury
Evaluating a resident's response to a new pain plan

rationale.correct: LPNs give medications and treatments to stable clients and reinforce teaching; RNs assess, plan and evaluate.

perOption.a: Giving medications to stable residents is within LPN scope.
perOption.b: Wound care for stable residents is within LPN scope.
perOption.c: LPNs reinforce teaching.
perOption.d: Initial assessment is an RN responsibility.
perOption.e: Care planning is an RN responsibility.
perOption.f: Evaluating the plan is an RN responsibility.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Assign tasks to an LPN in long-term care.

questions.stem: While scanning a client's wristband, the nurse realizes the medication in hand is for the client in the next bed. The barcode scanner stops the nurse before anything is given. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Nothing more, since the scanner caught it
File a near-miss report in the event system
Write about the near miss in the client's chart
Ask the client to report the near miss

rationale.correct: Near misses are reported to support a culture of safety.

perOption.a: Near misses are reported so the system can be fixed.
perOption.b: Near-miss reports help find system problems before someone is harmed.
perOption.c: Event reports are not part of the medical record.
perOption.d: Reporting is the nurse's responsibility.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A new graduate asks the nurse about incident (event) reports after a client fell on the unit. Which statements by the nurse are accurate? Select all that apply.

options.text: "They are completed for events that caused harm or could have caused harm."
"They describe what happened without blaming anyone."
"They are used to find patterns and improve safety."
"They are filed in the client's medical record."
"We write 'incident report filed' in the nurse's notes."
"The charge nurse fills them in rather than the staff involved."

rationale.correct: Incident reports are factual, kept out of the chart, completed by those involved and used for quality improvement.

perOption.a: They cover near misses as well as actual events.
perOption.b: Objective facts support system improvement.
perOption.c: Quality improvement relies on reporting data.
perOption.d: They are kept separate from the medical record.
perOption.e: The medical record does not mention the incident report.
perOption.f: The person who saw or was involved in the event files the report.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A medical unit has had three client falls in a month, all between 0200 and 0500 and all on the way to the bathroom. The nurse manager forms a quality improvement team. What should the team do first?

options.text: Start hourly rounding on the unit during the night shift
Collect data on each fall, including timing, medications and staffing
Put bed exit alarms on clients older than 65 at night
Retrain the night staff on the unit's fall-prevention policy

rationale.correct: Quality improvement begins by collecting and analyzing data to find causes; interventions are chosen to match the causes found.

perOption.a: Hourly rounding may be part of the solution, but it is chosen after the causes are known.
perOption.b: Gathering and analyzing data shows patterns and root causes before solutions are chosen.
perOption.c: Blanket alarms add alarm fatigue and may not match the cause.
perOption.d: Training assumes the cause is staff knowledge, which is not yet known.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client died after receiving a unit of ABO-incompatible blood that had been checked by only one nurse. How should this event be classified, and what review does it need?

options.text: A near miss that needs a staff huddle
A sentinel event that needs a root cause analysis
An expected complication that needs documenting
A practice issue that needs only nurse discipline

rationale.correct: Sentinel events, such as unexpected death or serious harm, need a root cause analysis focused on systems, not blame.

perOption.a: Harm reached the client, so this is not a near miss.
perOption.b: An unexpected death from a preventable error is a sentinel event, and a root cause analysis looks for system causes.
perOption.c: An ABO-incompatible transfusion is a preventable error, not an expected complication.
perOption.d: Focusing on one person misses the system failures that allowed the error.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse manager is explaining the facility's just culture policy to new staff after two medication events on the unit. Complete the sentence.

content.template: In a just culture, a nurse who made an honest mistake is {{b1}}, while a nurse who knowingly skipped a required safety check is {{b2}}.

options.text: supported, and the system is examined
disciplined so others learn from it
left alone, since no one intended harm
held accountable for reckless behavior
treated the same as an honest mistake
coached, since the check slowed care

rationale.correct: Just culture: console human error, coach at-risk behavior, and hold reckless behavior accountable.

perOption.b1:a: Human error is addressed by improving systems.
perOption.b2:a: Conscious disregard of safety rules calls for accountability.
perOption.b2:b: Just culture separates error from reckless behavior.
perOption.b2:c: Coaching fits at-risk behavior; knowingly skipping a required check is reckless.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The infection prevention committee reports that the unit's catheter-associated urinary tract infection (CAUTI) rate has doubled this quarter. Which change would most likely bring the rate down?

options.text: Changing indwelling catheters on a routine 7-day schedule
Nurse-driven removal of catheters that are no longer needed
Cleaning around the meatus with an antiseptic three times a day
Irrigating each catheter daily with sterile saline

rationale.correct: Catheter days drive CAUTI, so nurse-driven removal protocols lower rates.

perOption.a: Routine catheter changes are not recommended and add risk.
perOption.b: Removing catheters as early as possible is the most effective way to prevent CAUTI.
perOption.c: Routine antiseptic meatal care does not prevent CAUTI; soap-and-water hygiene is enough.
perOption.d: Routine irrigation opens the closed system and increases infection risk.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: Two nurses are arguing loudly at the nurses' station, where clients and visitors can hear, about how a shared assignment was split. What should the charge nurse do first?

options.text: Tell them to stop now and settle it on their own after the shift
Move the discussion to a private room and hear both nurses out
Report both nurses to the nurse manager for unprofessional conduct
Decide which nurse is right and reassign the clients straight away

rationale.correct: Address conflict promptly, privately and with both parties heard.

perOption.a: This avoids the conflict without resolving it.
perOption.b: Privacy and listening to both sides support a fair resolution.
perOption.c: Escalation may be needed later, but first the charge nurse tries to resolve it.
perOption.d: Deciding without hearing both sides is unfair.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A new graduate tells the charge nurse that an experienced nurse often rolls their eyes and makes belittling comments about the new graduate in front of clients. What should the charge nurse do?

options.text: Tell the new graduate this is part of fitting in on a busy unit
Take the report seriously and follow the policy on incivility
Raise the behavior with the experienced nurse at the team huddle
Change the schedules so the two nurses work different shifts

rationale.correct: Incivility and bullying are safety issues and must be addressed through policy, not tolerated or avoided.

perOption.a: This dismisses lateral violence, which harms safety and retention.
perOption.b: Lateral violence is addressed through policy and leadership.
perOption.c: Public confrontation is unprofessional and can make things worse.
perOption.d: Avoidance does not address the behavior.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: At the start of a night shift, a medical unit nurse is given seven clients, including two who are receiving titrated infusions. The nurse believes the assignment is unsafe. What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Refuse the assignment and leave the unit before taking report
Accept the assignment and tell no one, to avoid conflict
Raise the concerns with the charge nurse and ask for a change
Call the state board of nursing to report the staffing level

rationale.correct: Raise concerns about an unsafe assignment through the chain of command and document per policy, such as an assignment-despite-objection form.

perOption.a: Leaving can be seen as abandonment, and the clients still need care.
perOption.b: Unsafe staffing must be raised so it can be fixed.
perOption.c: Concerns go through the chain of command first; the nurse documents per policy if the assignment stands.
perOption.d: Internal channels are used first.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nurse manager is planning the move to a new electronic documentation system in 3 months. Which strategy best reduces staff resistance to the change?

options.text: Announce the change a week before go-live
Involve staff early, explain why, and train
Ask staff to learn it on their own time
Save questions until after go-live

rationale.correct: Change management: involve staff, explain the reason, and support learning.

perOption.a: Short notice increases resistance.
perOption.b: Taking part and understanding the reason reduce resistance.
perOption.c: This increases frustration.
perOption.d: Avoiding questions undermines trust.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A nursing student the nurse is precepting today asks to give IV push famotidine, which the student has not given before. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Let the student give it alone to build confidence
Review it together and watch the student give it
Refuse to let the student give any medications
Give it, and have the student chart the dose

rationale.correct: Supervise students when they perform new skills.

perOption.a: The student needs supervision with new skills.
perOption.b: Supervision keeps the client safe while the student learns.
perOption.c: Supervised practice is appropriate.
perOption.d: Students do not document care they did not give.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A 74-year-old client with heart failure who lives alone has been readmitted three times in 2 months, each time with fluid overload after missing medications. Which referral is most likely to reduce further readmissions?

options.text: Case management for transitional care and follow-up
A dietitian consultation about a low-sodium diet
Cardiac rehabilitation after this hospital stay
A chaplain visit to support the client's coping

rationale.correct: Case management coordinates care across settings for high-risk clients and is the main tool for reducing readmissions.

perOption.a: Case managers coordinate follow-up visits, medications and home support across settings.
perOption.b: Diet teaching helps, but it does not address missed medications and follow-up.
perOption.c: Rehab improves fitness but does not address the reasons for readmission.
perOption.d: Spiritual support is helpful but does not address the causes of readmission.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Use case management to reduce readmissions.

questions.stem: A 38-year-old client newly diagnosed with type 1 diabetes has no health insurance and says, "I can't afford insulin or test strips." Discharge is planned for tomorrow morning, and the client lives alone. Which team member should the nurse contact?

options.text: Social worker
Diabetes educator
Dietitian
Pharmacist

rationale.correct: Social workers help clients overcome financial barriers and find community resources.

perOption.a: Social workers connect clients with financial assistance and community resources.
perOption.b: The educator teaches self-management but does not arrange financial help.
perOption.c: A dietitian helps with meal planning, not paying for supplies.
perOption.d: A pharmacist can suggest cheaper options but does not arrange financial assistance.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: A client recovering from a stroke is being transferred from the hospital to a skilled nursing facility this afternoon. Which action by the nurse is most important for continuity of care?

options.text: Give a report to the receiving nurse, including medications and recent changes
Send the client with a printed list of the hospital unit's phone numbers to call
Ask the client's daughter to explain the client's care to the facility staff
Skip the verbal report because the facility can read the chart online

rationale.correct: Transitions of care need a complete handoff, including medication reconciliation and recent changes.

perOption.a: A complete nurse-to-nurse handoff prevents errors at transitions of care.
perOption.b: A phone list does not pass on the information the next nurse needs.
perOption.c: The nurse is responsible for the handoff, not the family.
perOption.d: A direct handoff is still needed so the receiving nurse can ask questions.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is completing medication reconciliation for a client with diabetes and hypertension who is going home today. Which actions are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: Compare the home medications with the hospital medications
Ask about over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements
Give the client an updated, complete medication list
Clarify any discrepancies with the provider before discharge
Assume every home medication should continue as before
Skip reconciliation when the client takes fewer than three drugs

rationale.correct: Medication reconciliation at every transition prevents errors.

perOption.a: This finds omissions and duplications.
perOption.b: These can interact with prescriptions.
perOption.c: The client and the next providers need an accurate list.
perOption.d: Discrepancies must be resolved before the client leaves.
perOption.e: Each one must be reviewed for continuation.
perOption.f: Reconciliation is done for every client.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The hospital is full, and the medical unit has one negative-pressure isolation room left. Four clients waiting in the emergency department each need a private room. Which client should the nurse recommend for the negative-pressure room?

options.text: A client with a cough, night sweats and a cavity on the chest x-ray
A client with MRSA in a wound that is fully covered by a dressing
A client with Clostridioides difficile diarrhea and incontinence
A client with confirmed influenza who is coughing frequently

rationale.correct: Keep scarce negative-pressure rooms for airborne infections such as TB, measles and varicella.

perOption.a: Suspected pulmonary tuberculosis is airborne and needs the negative-pressure room.
perOption.b: Contact precautions can be used in an ordinary private room.
perOption.c: C. difficile needs contact precautions in a private room, not negative pressure.
perOption.d: Influenza needs droplet precautions, which an ordinary private room allows.

references: CDC infection control and isolation precautions guidance
NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.stem: The nurse is caring for three clients who each have a new problem. For each client, select the priority action.

cells.text: Client receiving IV vancomycin who has flushing and itching of the face and neck
Client 2 days after surgery with a red, swollen, tender calf
Client started on lisinopril yesterday who has swelling of the lips

options.text: Stop or slow the infusion and notify the provider
Give the PRN diphenhydramine and keep the rate
Apply cold packs to the face and neck
Keep the client in bed and notify the provider
Apply a warm compress and raise the leg
Encourage walking to improve blood flow
Hold the medication and assess the airway
Give the next dose with food
Document it as a minor side effect

rationale.correct: Recognize adverse reactions and complications quickly and act on the most dangerous part of each.

perOption.b1:a: This is an infusion-rate reaction; slowing or stopping the infusion relieves it.
perOption.b1:b: Antihistamines may help, but the rate must be reduced.
perOption.b1:c: This does not address the cause.
perOption.b2:a: Suspected DVT: limit movement of the leg until it is evaluated.
perOption.b2:c: Not until a DVT is ruled out.

references: NCSBN National Guidelines for Nursing Delegation; LaCharity, Prioritization, Delegation & Assignment
Rewritten to NCLEX-RN difficulty and reviewed by the content team on 19 November 2026.

questions.educationalObjective: Choose priority actions for several clients.

questions.stem: The nurse is planning the first hour of a busy shift with one assistive personnel. For each category, select the client who belongs there.

options.text: Client with a new irregular heart rate who feels dizzy
Client who needs a bed bath before a family visit
Client waiting for transport to radiology at 0900

groups.label: Can be delegated to the AP

options.text: Client who needs help filling out the lunch menu
Client who reports new chest pressure
Client who needs discharge teaching

rationale.correct: Urgent changes come first; routine tasks for stable clients can be delegated.

perOption.a: A new dysrhythmia with symptoms is urgent.
perOption.b: This is not urgent.
perOption.c: This is not urgent.

questions.stem: A nurse arrives for a day shift on a medical unit and is assigned five clients. The night nurse is ready to give report. Which action should the nurse take first?

Start the 0800 medications so they are not given late
Begin charting the morning assessments from the night notes
Restock the supply cart before the clients wake up

questions.stem: The nurse in an outpatient dialysis center is caring for four clients during treatment. Which client needs immediate attention?

options.text: A client who reports painful cramping in both calves 3 hours into treatment
A client whose potassium before treatment was 5.6 mEq/L, with no ECG changes
A client who suddenly has chest pain, shortness of breath and a cough
A client whose blood pressure is 128/76, down from 150/88 at the start

rationale.correct: Sudden chest pain and shortness of breath during dialysis can mean a life-threatening complication such as air embolism.

questions.stem: An assistive personnel (AP) refuses to help bathe a client on contact precautions for MRSA, saying, "I'm afraid I'll take it home to my baby." What should the nurse do first?

options.text: Report the AP to the nurse manager for refusing an assigned task
Explain how PPE and hand hygiene protect staff; offer to go in together
Do the client's care alone without discussing the fear with the AP
